quests.title: A Friend for the Road
quests.offer: You! {name}! Have you a moment for an old one's worry? Someone's gone off alone where they oughtn't. Will you [help]?
quests.summary: Old Mother Hesketh of Cotswold Village saw a young adventurer go off alone toward trouble - if only the old one could remember who it was.

steps.goal: Speak with Old Mother Hesketh in Cotswold Village
steps.say: Oh! You there - {name}, isn't it? You've the look of someone who knows which end of a sword is which. Listen, dear. Not an hour ago somebody went marching off down the south-east road after those cutpurses that have been robbing the farms. All on their own! Young, and far too pleased with themselves. It was a young... now, was it a [man]? Or was it a [woman]? Dear me. My eyes aren't what they were.

steps.goal: Find the reckless adventurer at the cutpurses' camp, south-east of Cotswold
steps.text: The last of the cutpurses scatters into the hedges. From behind the cart, the one you came for climbs out - bruised, scraped, and grinning.

stages.name: Rook the Cutpurse Captain
stages.announce: Behind a toppled cart someone is shouting for help - the cutpurses have them cornered. Their captain turns, grinning. 'Another hero? We'll have your purse as well.'

steps.goal: Speak with the adventurer you saved
steps.say:
Light above, that was close! I had them, you know. Right up until I didn't. I'm {cname} - and you're {name}? Old Mother Hesketh sent you, didn't she. She worries.

I owe you my life, and I don't like owing. So here's a thought: I was a fool to come out here alone, and I'll not make that mistake twice. Let me come with you. I'll watch your back, and you can keep me from doing anything this stupid again. What do you say? [Come along, then] [Glad to have you]

steps.goal: Speak with Old Gunnar One-Ear in Mularn
steps.say: Eh? Oh, it's you - {name}. I know that face, I never forget a face. Ears, now, ears I forget. Ha! Listen. Somebody went off east along the shore this morning, after the raiders that have been bothering the fishermen. Alone! The young never listen. It was a... hm. A [man], was it? Or a [woman]? Bah. My one good eye is getting worse than the other one.

A man! Yes - yes, a young man, I'm sure of it now. He looked like one of those... oh, what do you call them...
